selected_frontier.reason: A concurrent main commit added PYTHONSAFEPATH=1 to the Clay GO import-path receipt workflow. Review was needed to distinguish narrow script-path hardening from full Python import provenance and to check whether the SQLite V6 admission boundary already uses the stronger isolation primitive.
duplicate_avoidance: Did not duplicate the concurrent SQLite productive-process identity experiment recorded at research main 9e5baa67490ef993a4795388cc8c47713ac6fa55.
Did not modify Frank main because another worker changed the same import-path workflow during this cycle.

observed_reality.replication_scope: temporary fixtures on self-hosted Ubuntu; not 20 distinct production scripts

hypothesis: PYTHONSAFEPATH/-P is useful against implicit script-directory prepend but is not a complete import-provenance boundary because caller-controlled PYTHONPATH remains effective.
strongest_counterhypothesis: Setting PYTHONSAFEPATH=1 globally is sufficient for the relevant Frank admission paths because no attacker-controlled PYTHONPATH can reach them or because stronger isolation is already used at those boundaries.

go_out_of_box.name: PYTHONPATH_SHADOW_AFTER_SAFE_PATH
go_out_of_box.description: Use three same-named modules: script-directory shadow, intended dependency, and an adversarial PYTHONPATH shadow. Compare ordinary script execution, -P execution with intended PYTHONPATH, -P execution with adversarial PYTHONPATH prepended, and isolated -I control.

results.minus_I_with_external_paths: external dependency import rejected as expected

go_out_of_box.interpretation: -P removes the unsafe implicit prefix but does not ignore PYTHONPATH; -I additionally ignores PYTHON* environment variables. This is a negative result against treating safe-path alone as a full provenance boundary.

external_primary_evidence.finding: -P / PYTHONSAFEPATH prevents prepending a potentially unsafe path to sys.path; isolated mode -I implies -E and -P and therefore ignores PYTHON* environment variables.

counterevidence_and_scope.sqlite_v6_boundary: The current V6 SQLite launcher already executes its guard as /usr/bin/python3 -I -S, so the adversarial PYTHONPATH counterworld does not establish a new defect in that admission boundary.
counterevidence_and_scope.workflow_patch: The new PYTHONSAFEPATH=1 remains useful defense-in-depth for non-isolated workflow helper Python, but it must not be promoted as equivalent to isolated execution.
counterevidence_and_scope.replication_correction: The 20/20 import-path counts are repetitions of one temporary fixture lane, not evidence that 20 distinct Frank production scripts are vulnerable.

grf_collapse.test_delta: When Python invocation itself is security-sensitive, distinguish safe-path hardening from environment isolation and test explicit PYTHONPATH countercontrols.

No claim that -P is equivalent to -I
